I do agree though, when looking at art that is clearly AI generated, it is less interesting, but I cant guarantee that isnt also cause I see the loud minority constantly downing it, and subconsciously it has rubbed off on me in a way. replies.author: More_Argument_2494
replies.body:
Tbh I use ai to learn quite a lot. One example is ill ask AI to generate me a code blocks or more, with multiple mistakes either wrong commands, or in efficiencies, then attempt to fix it. Once the code I think is fixed is resubmitted it scores me and can then point out what I missed, or ways to further optimise.

Ai is more useful than any search engine, and the moralities around using it should be based on how it is used, not whether it is used at all. Even then, trying to just fully generate code or assets when you know nothing of the subject is going to be subpar and inefficient, it's more like an extra tool in your toolbox than something to replace the toolbox entirely

replies.author: ratthew
replies.body:
Tbh. I think the "tells" of AI game dev will be just as obvious as they are with web dev and design in general. It's just that there aren't enough games actually released with AI to be able to feel the similarities in those game mechanics that AI commonly reaches for.

Same goes for design / code (especially in web), you can only tell it's AI if you let the AI make "creative decisions", which usually results in the same go-to solution that's baked in the training data.

replies.author: syn_krown
replies.body: Ok, I can pick up what you're putting down, but an amazing app with an AI UI, shouldn't be discriminated against like its a race. A person might have an awesome idea for an app, something new, but the interface has a basic Aai look. Why should that take away from it?

replies.author: ratthew
replies.body:
The video demonstrates how irrational a loud minority reacts if they even just "sense" AI, even if it's not even there. Now you can imagine how they react if it's obvious.

People will be able to tell some way or another, and that will make them judge it harsher or not even give it a try because it makes it feel like there was no effort put into it. Same thing happened before AI as well just a little less widespread (I remember people not playing or downvoting games that had the "made with unity" splash screen).

I think if you're putting something out there, take the time to put effort into every part, make sure the AI does not decide on stuff, even if you don't want to deal with it. (especially stuff that you can see (UI) or feel (game play))

comments.author: ishmaellius
comments.body:
I think in about 10 or maybe 20 years, people will come to accept that there are two things going on here.  There is the thing itself - whether that's art, music, games, movies, what have you - and then there is human performance of it.  And those two things are wholly separate. 

People will eventually come to realize the thing itself is either enjoyable to them or not.  It's why even though a lot of people love a fancy meal, the very same people still also love a fast food hamburger.  Things are either something you enjoy, or not.

Then there is the aspect of human involvement - which I'm now calling Performance.  This is wholly different from the thing itself.  It's why you can go to an elementary school play of The Nutcracker and enjoy it, while also enjoying a world class symphony performing the same play, AND you may not mind listening to a recording of it from Spotify.

I think people are generally full of shit when they talk about AI Slop.  The truth is humans fucking love slop.  It's all around us, and has been ever since humans figured out how to make expensive shit cheaper. 

Eventually, people will realize they can love something regardless of how it was made, AND they can also love and appreciate a humans rendition of the very same thing... Eventually...

For now though... Idiots are gonna keep conflating the two.

I am not of the opinion AI can never make technically impressive work or inherently lacks soul. A lot of it is 'soulless' though from lack of taste. As you pointed out the cape heroes movies are practically ai.

I think its a clash of values though, people are recognising ai systems can produce Monet's (some probably worth looking at) and getting mad at that development. Not everyone cares about the journey of the artist or stories behind a work. I value the connection works have to people on top of it as an achievement. 

For instance we have statues preserved from the ancient Assyria, with technology we can probably laser cut/cnc exact replicas. Yet if you blew up the exact replica no one would care, the original being destroyed would elicit mourning, at least from people who imagine the ancient guy chipping away at the stone block and where the artifact came from. I think AI proponents would tend discount that value.
